changeSet.author: nexus-tk070.p6a
changeSet.comment:
chunks.metadata: backfill NULL to '{}'::jsonb (0 live at census time; unconditional), then DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb + SET NOT NULL.
RESTRICTED to octet_length(chash) = 32 rows (the exact predicate chunks_chash_octet_check enforces, rdr180-001-bytea-chash.xml): an UNRESTRICTED UPDATE re-validates EVERY CHECK constraint on every row it touches (ordinary Postgres semantics — unlike ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL, which does not rewrite tuples and checks nothing but the named column), and rdr180-001 deliberately left that constraint NOT VALID against pre-existing 16-byte legacy rows ("existing rows are 16-byte legacy until the rekey ... deliberately NOT a boot changeset" — its own header). Before this file, NOTHING in the whole changelog chain ever UPDATEs such a row, so the violation stays latent; an unrestricted backfill here would be the first thing to crash on it — SchemaUpgradeRehearsalIntegrationTest's aged-box rehearsal caught this exactly as designed.
Any row STILL metadata IS NULL after the restricted UPDATE can only be legacy-width (un-rekeyed): DELETE it, counted and RAISE NOTICE'd. This is the nexus-lgdel deletion arc — the 32-byte cutover has no path back, so an un-rekeyed row's content is unresolvable by construction, not merely inconvenient. A cleanup migration warns loudly, deletes, and proceeds; it never gates the upgrade on a legacy population it cannot fix in place.
FK ordering: catalog_document_chunks.fk_catalog_chunks_chunk (catalog-029-manifest-chunk-fk.xml) references chunks(tenant_id, collection, chash) with no explicit ON DELETE clause -- Postgres defaults that to NO ACTION, not CASCADE -- and catalog_document_chunks's own legacy-row cleanup does not run until hygiene-001-8, later in this same file. Deleting a doomed chunks row here, before that cleanup has run, would be rejected outright by the FK. So this changeset deletes the referencing catalog_document_chunks rows itself, first, in the same transaction, before touching the chunks parent rows. topic_assignments_chunk_fk (taxonomy-012-doc-id-chunk-fk.xml) is ON DELETE CASCADE and needs no such handling.
DELETE PREDICATE (review round, critic census finding): both deletes below key DIRECTLY on octet_length(chash) <> 32 OR chash IS NULL -- not on "metadata IS NULL", which was only a proxy true by the census's historical fact that 0 well-formed rows carried NULL metadata at census time. A direct chash-width check is correct regardless of any row written between census and this changeset actually running. The `OR chash IS NULL` arm is a genuine NULL hole in Postgres's three-valued logic: octet_length(NULL) <> 32 evaluates to NULL, not TRUE, so a bare octet_length(chash) <> 32 predicate would silently SKIP a null-chash row rather than catching it (chash is NOT NULL by schema today, so this arm cannot currently fire — it is defensive completeness, not a live case). Census fact (T2 hygiene-001-predicted-walk-counts-2026-08-29): 0 non-32-byte chash rows on the cloud in either table today; every live row is already width 32.
changeSet.sql: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'; LOCK TABLE nexus.chunks, nexus.catalog_document_chunks IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE;

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE nexus.chunks ALTER COLUMN metadata DROP NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE nexus.chunks ALTER COLUMN metadata DROP DEFAULT;

changeSet.author: nexus-tk070.p6a
changeSet.comment: catalog_collections.created_at: the engine has NEVER written it (CatalogRepository only SELECTs F_COL_CRTAT; live 260/260 NULL) — backfilled to the earliest indexed_at of the collection's own documents where derivable, else migration time, then SET NOT NULL DEFAULT now(). Both catalog_collections (the DML target) and catalog_documents (read via the correlated subquery) carry FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so both are toggled (aspects-004-1 precedent: toggling only the target leaves the join yielding zero rows for the non-bypass owner) — toggled in this order, restored in reverse (LIFO).

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE nexus.catalog_collections ALTER COLUMN created_at DROP NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE nexus.catalog_collections ALTER COLUMN created_at DROP DEFAULT;

changeSet.author: nexus-tk070.p6a
changeSet.comment:
catalog_document_chunks.chunk_index: backfill NULL to the row's own `position` (its documented duplicate; 22,298 / 7.8% live NULL at census time — the wire field predates this guarantee), then SET NOT NULL. The manifest write path (CatalogRepository#insertManifestChunkRows) is fixed in the same commit to fall back to `position` when a client omits chunk_index, so the population cannot re-accumulate.
RESTRICTED to octet_length(chash) = 32 rows, same reasoning as hygiene-001-5: an UNRESTRICTED UPDATE re-validates every CHECK constraint on every touched row, including the NOT VALID catalog_document_chunks_chash_octet_check (rdr180-001-bytea-chash.xml) left unenforced against pre-existing 16-byte legacy rows. Any row STILL chunk_index IS NULL after the restricted UPDATE can only be legacy-width (un-rekeyed): DELETE it, counted and RAISE NOTICE'd (nexus-lgdel deletion arc — no path back past the 32-byte cutover). This table has no downstream FK dependents (confirmed: nothing in the changelog chain references catalog_document_chunks), so no ordering hazard analogous to hygiene-001-5's applies here; some of the rows this DELETE targets may already be gone via hygiene-001-5's own FK-safety cleanup of manifest rows referencing a doomed chunks row — harmless overlap, the second DELETE simply finds nothing left to remove for those. An orphan manifest row (legacy-width chash with no matching chunks row at all) is NOT covered by hygiene-001-5's join-based cleanup; this changeset's own direct chash-width predicate (below) catches that case independently.
DELETE PREDICATE (review round, critic census finding): keys DIRECTLY on octet_length(chash) <> 32 OR chash IS NULL — not on "chunk_index IS NULL", which was only a proxy true by the census's historical fact. See hygiene-001-5's comment for the full rationale (identical NULL-hole and census-fact note; 0 non-32-byte chash rows on the cloud today).
changeSet.sql: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'; LOCK TABLE nexus.catalog_document_chunks IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE;

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE nexus.catalog_document_chunks ALTER COLUMN chunk_index DROP NOT NULL;

changeSet.author: nexus-tk070.p6a
changeSet.comment: BEFORE INSERT trigger: chunk_index defaults to position when a caller omits it. A plain column DEFAULT cannot reference a sibling column (position), so this is the DDL-level equivalent of the ""/0 column DEFAULTs step 4 added for catalog_documents — the row-level backstop for the WIDESPREAD raw-SQL manifest fixture pattern across the test suite (mirrors updated-at-001's SECURITY INVOKER trigger-function template) and a second line of defense behind CatalogRepository#insertManifestChunkRows' application-level fallback (same commit).

rollback.sql: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_catalog_document_chunks_chunk_index_default ON nexus.catalog_document_chunks; DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus.default_chunk_index_from_position();
